newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch AEX slides on profit-takers in index heavies.
newsitem.headline: Dutch AEX slides on profit-takers in index heavies.

text.p: Dutch shares widened losses in the last hour of trade to close well down on Tuesday, undermined by the check in the dollar's upward march and Wall Street's lacklustre start.
The AEX blue chip index shed 17.93 points or 1.81 percent to finish at 974.96, back from Monday's all-time record close.
But dealers said the losses were not underpinned by major trading volumes, with profit-taking in index heavyweights making the retreat seem worse than it really was.
"There's nothing fundamentally wrong," one said. "Investors are just cashing in on the recent runaway gains in some stocks."
Trading volumes were relatively low throughout the day, with many market players initially hanging back to await U.S. employment costs, which came in right on target.
Nevertheless the figures were a cue for some investors to take profits in AEX stocks which have been enjoying a particularly good run in recent days.
Steel maker Hoogovens, which recently accelerated its steady uptrend on reports of burgeoning European steel demand, dropped 2.30 guilders to 132.50 after hitting a high of 138.50 earlier in the day.
DSM, due to report first-half results tomorrow, also fell.
Having opened a guilder higher at 235.00, the shares picked up a further 0.50 in early trade before falling victim to profit taking. The chemicals stock closed 4.00 guilders down at 230.00.
Sector rival Akzo Nobel, also tipped to showcase sharply higher second-quarter profits when it reports on Thursday, similarly reversed early gains to close down 2.00 guilders at 303.00.

Also weighing heavily on the index was the 3.20 guilder loss to 111.60 of Royal Dutch Petroleum, while paper maker KNP BT bucked the cyclical reversal to finish up 0.30 guilders at 49.00 ahead of first half results on Thursday.

Philips' bull-run on the back of last week's well-received second-quarter figures ended with a 4.90 guilder loss to 163.90. "That's a major factor pressuring the index today," a dealer said, adding a lack of special incentives to steer the market had contributed to the overall listless sentiment.
Foods group Nutricia continued its march ahead, however, adding 8.40 guilders to 355.50 after a gain of 6.10 guilders yesterday.
Dealers said there was no new news in the market to underpin the stock's rise, other than that it was rated as one of the best buys in its sector.
